Haven't been able to contribute much lately, but an MRP would be the most helpful to test locally if I do find the time!

Are there any cyclic dependencies between these classes? Such as a superclass referring to the subclass in any way at all? Wondering whether that's interfering with figuring out the class hierarchy in docgen.

It sounds like you're really close to figuring out what the issue is!

It will be harder to inspect the stack & memory if you have any optimizations enabled. We generally suggest passing the `-dev_build=yes dev_mode=yes` to `scons` when building for engine development, which disables optimizations, adds debug symbols, sets more warnings, etc! Could also be the IDE having trouble knowing how to read the memory - I've personally had good luck with Visual Studio Community working well out of the box!

> but I did notice that the import process seemed to properly report the parent class of a class which exports the wrong parent to XML; it's in _generate_docs that I can see things give a different result.

The lines you tagged are likely the starting point to figuring out where the issue lies! Either it's selecting wrong information when the right information is available, or we only have wrong information and have to figure out where it's being set and fix that!

Your edit also has interesting information. GDScript should be able to figure out dependencies and compile/docgen them before their dependents, but maybe that isn't happening for some reason. It sounds like the docgen process of the subclasses is relying on the docgen process of the parent class, but the order isn't being respected, leading to default class hierarchy like `RefCounted` being used? 🤔

Alright, I have managed to make a proper MRP, and it *is* actually a cyclic dependency issue, just not the kind I was thinking about (it's not simply that ClassB inherits from ClassA which in turn references ClassB, but rather that another class is included in the dependency).

In the attached MRP below (.godot directory not included), loading starts alphabetically with the `some_class` folder, and the first file is `base_class.gd`. A function in this class checks for `MyScene.SOME_PATH`, so we have a dependency to `my_scene.gd`, which contains a `Dictionary[String, BaseClass]`, linking back to `base_class.gd`. Since the dictionary also contains a reference to `ChildClass1`, we have a dependency to the corresponding script, which itself of course depends on `base_class.gd`, and documentation is generated for `ChildClass1`. Same story for `ChildClass2`, then `MyScene` can be generated, and finally all dependencies for `BaseClass` are satisfied.

I added the following print statements to follow along:
* `"load " + p_path` at [`ResourceLoader::_load`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/19bb18716ef08b811fec330cba4d35fbdb027bcc/core/io/resource_loader.cpp#L314)
* `"dep (" + p_owner + ") " + E` at [`GDScriptCache::finish_compiling`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/19bb18716ef08b811fec330cba4d35fbdb027bcc/modules/gdscript/gdscript_cache.cpp#L423)
* `"gen " + doc.name` at [`GDScriptDocGen::_generate_docs`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/19bb18716ef08b811fec330cba4d35fbdb027bcc/modules/gdscript/editor/gdscript_docgen.cpp#L342)

Which produces the following:
```
load res://src/some_class/base_class.gd
dep (res://src/some_class/base_class.gd) res://src/my_scene.gd
dep (res://src/my_scene.gd) res://src/some_class/base_class.gd
dep (res://src/my_scene.gd) res://src/some_class/some_child_1.gd
dep (res://src/some_class/some_child_1.gd) res://src/some_class/base_class.gd
gen ChildClass1
dep (res://src/my_scene.gd) res://src/some_class/some_child_2.gd
dep (res://src/some_class/some_child_2.gd) res://src/some_class/base_class.gd
gen ChildClass2
gen MyScene
gen BaseClass
```

* Generating XML files with `doctool`:
    ```

    ```
    The XML themselves are correct for this project (`<class name="ChildClass1" inherits="BaseClass"`). This is not the case with some of my own projects, where I instead get `inherits="RefCounted"` or some other class, instead of my custom class).
* Opening the project in the editor:
    ```
    ❯ godot -e
    Godot Engine v4.7.beta.custom_build.321b8c944 (2026-05-15 20:42:10 UTC) - https://godotengine.org
    Vulkan 1.4.335 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT (RADV NAVI31)
    
    load  res://src/some_class/base_class.gd
    dep ( res://src/some_class/base_class.gd )  res://src/my_scene.gd
    dep ( res://src/my_scene.gd )  res://src/some_class/base_class.gd
    dep ( res://src/my_scene.gd )  res://src/some_class/some_child_1.gd
    dep ( res://src/some_class/some_child_1.gd )  res://src/some_class/base_class.gd
    gen  ChildClass1
    dep ( res://src/my_scene.gd )  res://src/some_class/some_child_2.gd
    dep ( res://src/some_class/some_child_2.gd )  res://src/some_class/base_class.gd

    gen  BaseClass
    ```

    The in-editor help wrongly displays the following inheritance tree for `ChildClass1`:
    `Inherits: RefCounted < Object` instead of `Inherits: BaseClass < RefCounted < Object`

The scripts load in a different order, which is enough to break the doc generation. When running in the editor, ChildClass1 and ChildClass2 depend on BaseClass, which is already queued for doc generation, so they get generated, but are missing BaseClass in the inheritance tree. On the other hand, `doctool` generates BaseClass first because of the different loading order, so the child classes are correctly picking up BaseClass in the inheritance tree. Maybe docs that get generated while not having all their dependencies satisfied should be tracked, and generated again later?

* `godot --doctool --gdscript-docs res://`

The scripts are still loaded in a different order for the editor and doctool, but this MRP ensures they both fail to find `BaseClass` as the parent class for `Parent2`. In both cases, we end up looking for the `BaseClass` dependency in `Parent2`, but `BaseClass` is already in the "wait list" from `Parent1`, so `Parent2` gets generated first. The rest of the dependencies gets resolved properly, and when `Parent1`'s turn comes, `BaseClass` is already properly generated.

I haven't tried to confirm it at this point, but it looks like the editor loads scripts in alphabetical order, and doctool in reverse alphabetical order? (not entirely sure as `parent_1.gd` gets loaded before `parent_2.gd`, but `my_scene.gd` and `child_2.gd` coming after it look like reverse alphabetical order).

@dalexeev Coming back to [your comment from last year](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106256#discussion_r2083402155), with my previous post here, I've now tracked down what I believe is the closest point to the problem. As mentioned above, the dependency chain goes `get_full_script()`, `reload()`, `compile()`, and `finish_compiling()`, but when the problematic script checks its own dependencies, one of the scripts is also a dependency for another script, and as such is already in the `full_gdscript_cache`, which means the `get_full_script()` call for that dependency [returns early](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/df6235838b63dd49f448547406e339848455c140/modules/gdscript/gdscript_cache.cpp#L358).

At that point, the dependencies are considered resolved, the problematic script then calls `generate_docs()`, however documentation for its dependencies has not been generated, but `_generate_docs()` still assumes `doc` to contain valid data (and that's the part your comment was referring to).
